NetCoreNOC champion-agreement report
==============================================================

How well the BUILT-IN SCORER already agrees with the operators, at bag
level, conditioned. This report trains nothing and involves no model.

  AGREEMENT IS NOT CORRECTNESS. There is no ground truth here — only what
  an operator said about a grouping they were shown. A high rate means the
  champion and the operators concur; it does not mean either was right.

-- population ------------------------------------------------
  labelled bags, all provenance               13
  labelled bags, provenance=current           12
  merge-aware incidents among them            12
  distinct operators                           3
  bags with no promoted pair                   1
  promoted pairs behind them                1885
  verdict: confirm                             8
  verdict: split                               4

  EVERY FIGURE BELOW EXCEPT THE PROVENANCE SECTION IS OVER `current` ROWS
  ALONE. `legacy_capture` labels were acquired before v0.7.5 repaired the
  click path: they are of UNKNOWN quality, which is weaker than bad, and
  blending them into a headline would make it uninterpretable in a way no
  reader could detect afterwards.

-- THE HEADLINE ----------------------------------------------
  champion agreement      n=   12  confirmed=    8    66.7%  [ 33.3,  91.7]

  The interval is a CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP OVER INCIDENTS, not over bags and
  never over pairs: two labels on situations that were merged into one are
  ONE incident. Below 10 incidents it is REFUSED outright and
  prints `n/a` — resampling a handful of clusters gives an interval that
  looks like a measurement and is an artefact of a handful of numbers.

  READ THE DECOMPOSITION, NOT THIS LINE. An aggregate of 94% that is 99% on
  uniform storm bags and 58% on mixed bags is the difference between an ML
  programme with no headroom and one with a clear target.

-- by MIXED vs UNIFORM bag (the strongest cut) ---------------
  mixed                   n=    3  confirmed=    2    66.7%  [interval n/a]
  uniform-accept          n=    6  confirmed=    5    83.3%  [interval n/a]
  uniform-reject          n=    2  confirmed=    0     0.0%  [interval n/a]
  no-pairs                n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]

  A UNIFORM BAG CONTAINED NO DECISION. Every pair in it fell on the same
  side of the threshold, so the operator confirmed an outcome the champion
  could not have reached differently: the confirm says nothing whatever
  about the scorer's judgement. A MIXED bag spans the threshold — there the
  champion made a call, and there alone the agreement rate is about it.
  Measured over the eval corpus, 7 of 9 scenarios are uniform.

-- by bag size -----------------------------------------------
  1                       n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]
  2                       n=    3  confirmed=    1    33.3%  [interval n/a]
  3-5                     n=    5  confirmed=    3    60.0%  [interval n/a]
  6-10                    n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]
  11-50                   n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]
  51+                     n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]

  CONFIRMATION STRENGTH DECAYS WITH SIZE. An operator confirming a
  five-hundred-member storm did not verify one hundred and twenty-four
  thousand pairs; one confirming two members verified the only pair there
  was. `unrecorded` is a pre-v0.8.0 label, distinguishable from a zero.

-- by storm --------------------------------------------------
  quiet                   n=    5  confirmed=    2    40.0%  [interval n/a]
  partly                  n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]
  storm                   n=    5  confirmed=    4    80.0%  [interval n/a]
  no-pairs                n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]

  IN A STORM THE CHAMPION IS RIGHT ABOUT SOMETHING IT COULD NOT HAVE GOT
  WRONG. Accept rates measured at 0% on quiet corpus traffic and 100% in
  every storm scenario, so a storm confirm is close to tautological.
  `partly` is a bag whose pairs straddle the storm boundary; it is given
  its own row rather than assigned by a majority rule, because the
  threshold such a rule would need is a number nobody measured.

-- by visibility scope ---------------------------------------
  full view               n=   10  confirmed=    7    70.0%  [ 40.0, 100.0]
  restricted              n=    2  confirmed=    1    50.0%  [interval n/a]

  A SCOPED EDITOR JUDGED A PARTIAL VIEW and cannot say which part — the
  redaction deliberately carries no NE id, address or entity key. The
  resulting noise is SYSTEMATIC, not random: it correlates with the scope
  policy, so it does not average out with more data.

-- by operator -----------------------------------------------
  (unattributed)          n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]
  operator 1              n=    4  confirmed=    3    75.0%  [interval n/a]
  operator 2              n=    4  confirmed=    2    50.0%  [interval n/a]
  operator 3              n=    3  confirmed=    2    66.7%  [interval n/a]

  A HEADLINE OVER THREE PEOPLE IS THREE PEOPLE'S OPINION. Spread here is
  not noise to be averaged away — it is the quantity that says whether
  `confirm` means the same thing to two operators.
  OPERATORS ARE ANONYMISED and the aliases are ordered by bag count, not by
  identity. What this cut is for is the spread; a name would turn a bias
  measurement into a per-employee performance report nobody consented to.

-- by capture provenance (NEVER averaged) --------------------
  current                 n=   12  confirmed=    8    66.7%  [ 33.3,  91.7]
  legacy_capture          n=    1  confirmed=    0     0.0%  [interval n/a]

  The one section computed over ALL rows, because separating the two
  populations is its entire purpose. If these two rates differ materially,
  the pre-v0.7.5 click path is visible in the data and the `current` rate
  above is the only one worth quoting.

-- by promotion coverage -------------------------------------
  full                    n=   11  confirmed=    7    63.6%  [ 36.4,  90.9]
  none                    n=    1  confirmed=    1   100.0%  [interval n/a]

  `partial` is NOT an edge case: the sliding window and MAX_CANDIDATES mean
  pairs within a labelled situation may never have been evaluated. A bag
  with coverage `none` or `empty` has no promoted pair, so it appears in
  the `no-pairs` row of the cuts above — counted, never silently dropped.

-- what this report CANNOT tell you --------------------------
  * whether the champion was RIGHT. Only whether an operator agreed.
  * whether a disagreement was the scorer's fault. A `split` may mean the
    grouping was wrong, or that the operator wanted a different grouping
    for an operational reason this system never sees.
  * anything about situations nobody labelled. Operators label what they
    open, and this measures what they labelled.
  * anything about pairs that were never evaluated. They are absent by
    construction; the coverage section counts them, and that is all.
  * how much headroom a model has. It bounds it from above on the labelled
    population and says nothing about the rest of the network.
